solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Steps to block change producing disease

indicators.note: one thing set to block another sits inside it, so the steps go into the change

parts.note: small change, coins, can be pence
a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone reshuffling stairs to stop a change in the building, oddly causing illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' wants to be a verb or the definition; it is the inserted piece, and 'to block' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly epidemic, an outbreak of plague, so a synonym for a disease.

clue.text: Pale old Caledonian gathers energy from moving about

indicators.note: a person who gathers something in holds it within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland, once called Caledonia
KE stands for kinetic energy, the energy of a body in motion

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot, pallid, gaining energy from walking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' is not pallor but a fence stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a pointed stake in a fence, as is a picket.

clue.text: Drink, with second available

parts.note: handy means available or close at hand

explanation.surface: Having a drink with a second one on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, so a type of drink.

clue.text: Bar delivery follows Italian team

indicators.note: the delivery follows the team, so comes after it

parts.note: Inter is the Milan football club Internazionale
diction is a manner of speaking, a delivery

explanation.surface: A pub's delivery comes after an Italian football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub; it is a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdiction is a formal prohibition, a ban or bar.

clue.text: Make Eric's partner broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Eric Morecambe called his comedy partner Ernie Wise Ern

explanation.surface: Getting Eric's comedy partner on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a British TV comedy double act; Eric's catchphrase name for Ernie was Ern.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Caught by policeman, hold criminal peasant

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within it

parts.note: copper is a slang word for a policeman

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A criminal peasant caught by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the cricket abbreviation C, but with 'by' it signals containment; 'criminal' makes the anagram LODH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy rustic, an insulting word for a peasant.

clue.text: Vulgar heartless fellow

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter, here the middle one of the five

parts.note: cheap can mean vulgar or tawdry

explanation.surface: A description of a coarse, unfeeling man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes E, the middle letter of CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal British word for a man, a synonym of fellow.

clue.text: Much-loved college was in debt

parts.note: a hall is a college or residence at a university
owed means was in debt

explanation.surface: A beloved college that ran up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means revered or sacred, so deeply honoured and much-loved.

clue.text: Organ in favour of the government

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the state is the government

explanation.surface: A newspaper, an organ, that supports the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a newspaper; it is a gland.
explanation.definitionFit: The prostate is a gland in the male body, a bodily organ.

clue.text: One will churn out speech and broach text for editing

indicators.note: text sent for editing gets reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer who talks endlessly and opens up a text to be edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for editing' rearranges the ten letters of BROACH TEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who talks incessantly, producing a stream of speech.

clue.text: See round satellite dish

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: An instruction to look around a satellite dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satellite dish' reads as one phrase but splits: the moon is wordplay, the food is the definition. 'round' reverses the word for see.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish stew, so a dish; also a medley.

clue.text: What spins frequently with-it pieces of music

definitions.text: What spins frequently with-it pieces of music

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
oft is a poetic word for often
hep is old slang for fashionable or with-it
ops is the plural abbreviation of opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A description of a show that regularly played trendy music.
explanation.walkthrough: Top of the Pops was a long-running BBC TV chart show where records were spun weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC chart show played the latest hit records every week, so it regularly spun fashionable songs.

clue.text: Last term, and university introduces Bible studies

indicators.note: the university comes first and so introduces what follows it

parts.note: an end is a term or limit
RE, religious education, is the school subject covering the Bible

explanation.surface: A last term at college, with the university bringing in Bible studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective with 'term'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to last or persist over time, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Drive off with solicitor following gun battle

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away an animal or person
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in that sense

explanation.surface: A lawyer drives away after a firefight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer; here it is one who touts for business.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out is a decisive exchange of gunfire, a gun battle.

clue.text: Dog that's more cunning guarding territory

indicators.note: one word guarding another surrounds it

parts.note: foxier means slyer, more cunning
TERR is an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A sly dog protecting its patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox terrier is a small breed of terrier, a type of dog.

clue.text: Navigator for aeroplane circling Cape in trial run

parts.note: a pilot guides ships or aircraft
pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: the aircraft goes round the cape, so its letters surround it

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A navigator flies a plane around a headland on a test flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot project is a small-scale trial run before a full launch.

clue.text: Officials make 10 poets lose their head

parts.note: clue 10 is a dish, and that dish is a kind of stew

indicators.note: losing the head drops the first letter

parts.note: bards are poets

explanation.surface: Officials making poets lose their heads, a beheading scene.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer to 10 Across, a dish, here a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are officials who manage an event, such as at a race meeting.

clue.text: Old queen with a husband appear round Eastern Terrace

indicators.note: these words appear round, that is surround, the next letter

parts.note: VR, Victoria Regina, is Queen Victoria's cipher
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria and her husband appear on an Eastern terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear round' is the containment signal: the queen, 'with', 'a' and husband together surround the Eastern letter, which lands second.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, a kind of terrace.

clue.text: Perfect score by Mozart

parts.note: a score is twenty
the composer is the answer to 20 Down, so stands for the number twenty

explanation.surface: Praise for a flawless musical score written by Mozart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' and 'Mozart' look musical; one is a count of twenty, the other names clue 20.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty vision is normal sharp eyesight, so the phrase means perfect or flawless.

clue.text: Pictures upset people in covert organisation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Images that disturb staff in a secret agency.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' flips the word upside down, giving NEM; 'Pictures' means the movies, not images.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is an informal name for the cinema, where films are shown.

clue.text: Composer has grounds for sale around Australia

indicators.note: the market goes around the next piece

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place for selling
Oz is an informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A composer selling his lands in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was the Austrian classical composer.

clue.text: Munitions any power deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are rearranged into position, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An army deploying munitions with whatever force it has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges ANY POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry means arms collectively, close to munitions, military weapons and ammunition.

clue.text: Player run out by Compton, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Denis Compton was a famous English cricketer
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricketer run out by Compton, largely his fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Denis Compton was an English cricketer of the 1940s-50s; 'mostly' drops the S of DENIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is a film actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Avoid star being around husband

indicators.note: one word being around another encloses it

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: Keeping away from a celebrity hanging around a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a celebrity; it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to deliberately avoid someone or something.

clue.text: Police officer trails about Liverpool

indicators.note: the officer trails, coming after the word for about

parts.note: re means about, concerning
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A detective follows leads around Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool Football Club are nicknamed the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reds is the nickname of Liverpool Football Club, from its red strip.

clue.text: Offering of Savoy Hotel a prig spurned

indicators.note: spurned, kicked away, suggests the letters are knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: A snobbish guest snubs the Savoy Hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy Theatre in London staged Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operettas. 'spurned' rearranges HOTEL A PRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Savoy operas of Gilbert and Sullivan are the classic example of the genre.

clue.text: Note old part of London

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A jotted reminder about an old district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in London's West End, an example of part of the city.

clue.text: Nuts start to hold back part of engine

parts.note: cranks are eccentrics, nuts

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Mechanical nuts begin holding back a piece of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks mechanical; it means eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: A crankshaft turns the pistons' motion into rotation, an engine component.
